data.source_title: Efficiency in the Endoscopy Unit: Can We “Turn Around” Room Turnover? An Observational Quality Improvement Study
data.locator: Methods, Definitions—Outcomes; Results, Table 4 (All procedures); cohort dates in Participants
data.source_setting: Single tertiary referral center in Toronto, Canada; outpatient endoscopy unit, two standard rooms plus a third used almost exclusively for advanced procedures
data.source_n: 750 routine outpatient endoscopic procedures included in Table 4 (all procedures); 803 cases met initial criteria before exclusions for pairwise analysis
data.quantity: Non-procedure interval: patient 1 scope-out to patient 2 scope-in
data.source_evidence_basis: The authors define non-procedure time (NPT) from patient 1 scope-out to patient 2 scope-in, encompassing processes outside the procedure. Across all 750 included procedures, median NPT was 19 minutes (IQR 16–22). The endpoint is not cleaning-only and may include setup, paperwork or delays.
data.limitations: Single outpatient endoscopy center; selection excluded inpatient, advanced and anesthesia cases, cases affected by patient/transport delays, and turnovers over 25 minutes (often scheduled breaks). Not hospital bed turnover or a general room-cleaning duration.
data.inferred_scenario_use: Use as an external procedure-room between-case elapsed-time benchmark only when modeling a comparable outpatient endoscopy workflow. Do not assign all 19 minutes to EVS or use it for inpatient/ED room readiness.

data.source_title: Efficiency in the Endoscopy Unit: Can We “Turn Around” Room Turnover? An Observational Quality Improvement Study
data.locator: Methods, Definitions—Outcomes; Results, Table 4 (All procedures); cohort dates in Participants
data.source_setting: Single tertiary referral center in Toronto, Canada; routine outpatient endoscopy
data.source_n: 750 routine outpatient endoscopic procedures included in Table 4 (all procedures)
data.quantity: Turnover time: patient 1 out of room to patient 2 into room
data.source_evidence_basis: The authors separately define turnover time (TT) as patient 1 out to patient 2 in. For all 750 included outpatient procedures, median TT was 6 minutes (IQR 4–9), compared with 19 minutes for the broader scope-out-to-scope-in NPT interval. The distinct endpoints show why TT should not stand in for all between-procedure elapsed time.
data.limitations: Same single-site outpatient endoscopy cohort and exclusions as the paired NPT record. TT is not a cleaning-only interval or inpatient bed-readiness measure; scheduled breaks and delay-related exclusions may affect observed values.
data.inferred_scenario_use: For comparable outpatient procedure-room scenarios, preserve TT and NPT as separate event intervals; do not infer room-cleaning duration or general hospital turnaround from either value.
